name.ja: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール

overview.en: Ferdinand de Saussure was a Swiss linguist whose ideas on the structure of language founded modern structural linguistics and influenced the entire field of semiotics.

early_life.en: Born in Geneva to a prominent scientific family, he published a groundbreaking work on Indo-European vowels at age twenty-one.

impact.en: His distinction between langue and parole, the concept of the sign as signifier and signified, and the synchronic approach to language study revolutionized linguistics and influenced structuralism across all humanities.

event.en: Published Memoir on the Primitive System of Vowels in Indo-European Languages at age 21
Began teaching the courses on general linguistics at the University of Geneva

description.en: Posthumous compilation of his lectures that founded modern structural linguistics

text.en: In language there are only differences without positive terms.
